prompt_text: Who is the best health insurance broker in Kansas City to help me pick a plan?
answer_verbatim:
I can’t name a single objectively “best” broker for everyone, because the right broker depends on whether you need Medicare, an individual/ACA marketplace plan, small‑group/employer coverage, or something else — and on whether you want an independent broker, a captive agent (tied to one insurer), in‑person help, bilingual service, etc.

I can help you find highly rated brokers in Kansas City if you tell me:
- Are you looking for Medicare (Part A/B/Advantage/Part D), an individual/ACA plan, or small‑group/business coverage?
- Do you live on the Missouri or Kansas side (or give your ZIP)?
- Prefer independent brokers (compare multiple carriers) or don’t mind a carrier agent?
- Any other needs (Spanish/other language, evening/weekend meetings, help with claims)?

If you want to search yourself, here’s a quick checklist and places to look:

Where to find brokers or free counselors
- Medicare.gov “Find local help” for Medicare SHIP counselors and certified agents.
- Healthcare.gov local help finder or your state marketplace (if looking for ACA plans).
- Missouri Division of Insurance and Kansas Insurance Department — license lookup to confirm an agent’s license.
- Google Maps/Yelp — read recent reviews and ratings.
- Local independent insurance agencies (search “independent health insurance agent Kansas City”).
- AARP and community health centers often have lists of trusted Medicare advisers.

What to ask a prospective broker
- Are you independent or do you represent a single carrier?
- Which carriers and plans do you regularly work with in Kansas City?
- How long have you helped people with my type of coverage?
- How are you paid (commission from carrier vs. client fee)?
- Will you help with enrollment, appeals, and claims after I enroll?
- Can you give references from other clients in KC?

Red flags
- Pressure to sign right away or steer only to one plan without comparing options.
- Refusal to disclose how they’re paid.
- Lack of a license or unwillingness to give their license/NPN number.

If you tell me the plan type and your ZIP or side of the city, I’ll pull up a short list of highly rated local independent brokers and free local counseling resources and can suggest a few to contact. Which type of plan do you need help with?
